critic_risk_flags: Fractional SEIRS with delayed_I and delay=3 adds both longer delay and fractional memory, increasing timing and memory flexibility simultaneously. With short single-season data, this is likely over-complex and weakly identifiable, especially around sharp peaks.

Fractional SEIRS with delayed_I (delay=2) matches the discovered family, but fractional memory is not clearly justified with only 31 training weeks and high peakiness; elevated risk of overfitting peak width/decay and reducing identifiability without adding observation alignment beyond the non-fractional counterpart.

Fractional SEIHR compounds two identifiability risks for short single-season data: an explicit H compartment (already flagged as weakly identifiable) plus fractional memory. High risk of overfitting peakiness and producing unstable parameterizations across rolling windows.
